transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. It is so very nice to meet you, too. Thank you for taking the time to see me. 

Um, well, I hope I'm not wasting your time, but... I suppose I came in because I just can't seem to get anything in order lately. It's a bit embarrassing to admit, really, because I've always tried my best to keep a nice home for my family. But... well, my kitchen table is just covered right now. It's gotten a bit cluttered with my husband's appointment papers, and some church flyers, and notes from the senior center... oh, and all these half-finished to-do lists I make. 

I sit down there meaning to sort it all out, and I just... I don't know which thing to do first. I just sort of stare at it, and then, before I know it, the whole day is just gone. I'm sure it sounds silly, and I really do try to stay on top of things, but... is that the sort of thing you help people with?
When you are sitting there staring at the papers, what is going through your mind?

Oh, goodness. I want to give you a helpful answer, Doctor, but... honestly? I'm not really sure. I hope that doesn't sound too foolish. 

It's almost like... well, my mind just goes a bit blank, or maybe a little fuzzy. I'll sit down thinking, 'I need to handle these flyers,' and then... I don't even really know where my thoughts go, to be perfectly honest with you. It's just a sort of fog, and then I'll realize I've just been looking out the window or staring at the pile without actually seeing it. 

I'm so sorry if that's not very specific. I really do try to focus on them. Is... is that an alright answer? I hope I'm explaining it properly for you.
Beyond this difficulty with focus, have you been feeling sad, down, or have you lost interest in the activities you usually enjoy?

Oh, no, no, not at all! I wouldn't say I've been feeling sad or down. I mean, everyone has a gloomy day here and there, of course, but overall I'm quite content. I still very much enjoy my time with my family and my little groups at the church. 

It's really just... just this silly business with the papers and the organizing that's been bothering me. I still love doing all my usual things, I just... well, I have a harder time getting around to them sometimes because I get so caught up in the muddle on the table. 

I hope that's a good thing, that I'm not feeling sad? I certainly don't want to complain when I have so much to be grateful for. Does that help rule out anything serious, Doctor?
Looking back at your life, have you always struggled with organizing your tasks and staying focused in this way, or is this something that has only started happening more recently?

Oh, dear. Well... I suppose if I am being completely honest with you—and I do want to give you all the right information—it isn't exactly a new problem. It's a little shameful to admit at my age, but... even way back when I was just a little girl, my teachers used to write on my report cards that I was a bright student. Which was very kind of them to say! But... well, they also wrote that I was a bit careless. 

I was always forgetting my reading books or leaving my homework behind at the house, and they constantly had to remind me to finish my seatwork before I could go outside to play. I always meant to do it right the first time, I really did. I just... lost track of myself, I suppose. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad child. I always tried to be good and polite for my teachers. Is it helpful for you to know about things from that far back, Doctor?
